shifts.summary: Candidates reported a mixed difficulty overall, with many finding the paper harder than expected. Reasoning had many statement based questions and a few coding‑decoding items, while GA was described as difficult by several sources. Quantitative section was largely difficult with many trigonometry and geometry problems. English was generally easy to moderate, though some tough vocabulary appeared.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Statement based questions were numerous, some coding‑decoding and matrix items appeared. Candidates mentioned both easy and tricky reasoning items, with attempts ranging from 22 to 24.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS portion was reported as hard, with many current affairs and constitutional questions. Some reports noted easy GA items, but the majority described difficulty.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant had a mix of easy and very hard items; many trigonometry, circle geometry and tangent problems were reported.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was generally doable with some tough vocabulary; passage based set was easy for most candidates.

observations: Pattern changed compared to previous years, with more statement based reasoning.
GA was the toughest section for many candidates.
Quantitative section mixed easy and very difficult items, especially trigonometry.
English remained the most approachable section overall.
disagreements: Overall difficulty reports split between Difficult and Easy to Moderate (two reports each).
English difficulty split between Easy and Easy to Moderate (three reports each).

Good‑attempt counts ranged from 68 to 75 overall, with section‑wise attempts between 11 and 23. Time management was a concern mainly in Quant, while Reasoning and English were viewed as manageable. Candidates noted a variety of topics including current affairs, space missions and advanced maths.

intro: On 22 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have reported analyses, indicating overall difficulty ranging from moderate to difficult, with varying section‑wise experiences. Unofficial good‑attempt counts are 75–85 for shift 1 and 68–75 for shift 2, but SSC normalises scores across shifts, so direct comparison should be cautious. Shift 3 remains pending, as sufficient candidate evidence has not yet been gathered.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as moderate to difficult, while shift 2 was reported as moderate overall. No difficulty assessment is available for shift 3 because the analysis is still pending.

faqs.q: How many candidates achieved good attempts in each shift on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: For shift 1, unofficial reports indicate 75–85 good attempts overall. Shift 2 shows an unofficial range of 68–75 good attempts overall. No good‑attempt data is available for shift 3 at this time.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered most challenging on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: In shift 1, candidates found Reasoning (especially statement‑based questions) and General Ability difficult, with Quantitative problems in trigonometry and geometry also noted as hard. Shift 2 highlighted time‑management challenges in Quantitative, while Reasoning and English were viewed as manageable.

faqs.q: Is there any time‑management issue reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Candidates in shift 2 reported difficulty managing time mainly in the Quantitative section. No specific time‑management concerns were highlighted for shift 1, and shift 3 has no published analysis yet.

faqs.q: When will analysis for shift 3 of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 22 October 2026 be available?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for shift 3 yet. Further candidate evidence is required before a review can be added, and no specific publication timeline can be provided.
